solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One taking up course extremely eager after stupid delay

indicators.note: the eager ends come after the stupid-plus-delay pieces

parts.note: dumb is an old word for stupid
to wait is to delay

indicators.note: the word eager is reduced to its two extremities

explanation.surface: Someone sluggish and keen is slow to take up a course of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' is a course of a meal, not of study: the lift carries dishes up.
explanation.definitionFit: A small lift carrying food between floors brings each course up from the kitchen.

clue.text: Renaissance artist engages a dull bit of brain

indicators.note: to engage is to hold within, so the artist's name wraps the other pieces

parts.note: Albrecht Dürer, German Renaissance painter and engraver
matt (or mat) describes a dull, unshiny finish

explanation.surface: A Renaissance painter takes on a tedious piece of anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: The tough outer membrane covering the brain is a part of it in anatomical terms.

clue.text: Fail to get money supply cut

parts.note: M1 is the economists' measure of narrow money supply, written here as MI
to shear is to cut

explanation.surface: A complaint that a reduced money supply means failing to get funds.
explanation.walkthrough: M1 (with the digit read as letter I) is a standard measure of money supply.
explanation.definitionFit: To mishear is to fail to catch, or get, what someone said.

clue.text: Think to take on spreading rat poison

indicators.note: the rearranged rat is taken on at the front of the thinking word
spreading out the letters of the word rat rearranges them

parts.note: to opine is to think or hold an opinion

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about tackling a rat infestation with poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat poison' reads as one phrase, but it splits: 'spreading' scrambles rat to ATR, and 'poison' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A toxic alkaloid from deadly nightshade, so it is a poison.

clue.text: No risk now the sea-fret has lifted?

definitions.meaning: the idiom says it is safe to proceed, nobody is watching
a sea-fret is a coastal fog, so literally the shoreline can now be seen

explanation.surface: Fog over the sea has cleared, so there is no more danger.
explanation.walkthrough: A sea-fret is a sea mist on Britain's east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom signals that danger has passed and one may safely go ahead.

clue.text: More optimistic about leaving bishop's staff

indicators.note: the about letter is leaving, so it is removed from the staff

parts.note: a crosier is the hooked staff a bishop carries
C stands for circa, about

explanation.surface: Things look brighter after quitting the bishop's employment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees, but it is the crook-shaped crosier.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosy means hopeful, so rosier is the comparative: more hopeful.

clue.text: Sign to approach stream

definitions.meaning: a northern English word for a brook

explanation.surface: A signal inviting someone down to the brook.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a summoning gesture and a northern English word for a brook.

clue.text: Pirate, thriller writer's said, always poetic

indicators.note: the writer's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: John Buchan wrote The Thirty-Nine Steps
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A pirate tale by a thriller writer, as poetic as ever.
explanation.walkthrough: John Buchan was a Scottish thriller writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer was a seventeenth-century Caribbean pirate.

clue.text: Team made smaller in bristling style?

parts.note: a crew is a team, as of rowers
cut means reduced

explanation.surface: A slimmed-down squad given a spiky look.
explanation.definitionFit: The very short haircut leaves the hair standing up like bristles.

clue.text: To find a new supplier is expedient

definitions.meaning: obtain supplies from a different place
a means or stratagem one can fall back on

explanation.surface: Switching suppliers is the practical move.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-source it means change supplier; as one word it is a useful stratagem.

clue.text: Confidence in both dry and wet

parts.note: sec is the wine term for dry
to ret flax is to soak it

explanation.surface: Assurance that holds good in drought and rain alike.
explanation.walkthrough: Retting is soaking flax or hemp to loosen its fibres.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidence is something told privately, a secret shared in trust.

clue.text: Shabby-sounding appearance

indicators.note: the shabby word is spoken, giving one that sounds identical

parts.note: mean can describe a poor, shabby place

explanation.surface: Someone looks rather down-at-heel.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's bearing or look, their outward appearance.

clue.text: Work history, a year in France in its southern region

indicators.note: the year word is put inside the region

parts.note: Provence is a region in the south of France
an is French for year

explanation.surface: A year spent in Provence becomes part of someone's employment record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' here is a work of art, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: The recorded origin and chain of ownership of an artwork.

clue.text: Inserts ad after confusing delay

indicators.note: the letters of inserts ad are jumbled, as in a confusion

explanation.surface: An advertisement is slipped in after a muddling hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateness is being slow or delayed, a noun for delay.

clue.text: Forty on board taking jacket before work

indicators.note: the jacket piece goes in front of the work piece

parts.note: a doublet is a close-fitting jacket of old
op, short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A forty-year-old on a committee puts on a jacket before getting to work.
explanation.walkthrough: On a dartboard the double ring of the 20 scores forty.
explanation.definitionFit: In darts, hitting the double segment at the top of the board scores forty.

clue.text: Romantic author last to attack food

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the word attack

parts.note: eats is slang for food

explanation.surface: A writer of love stories is the final one to tuck in.
explanation.walkthrough: Romantic means of the Romantic poets.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats was a leading English poet of the Romantic movement.

clue.text: Being ready to ride is added plus to jockey

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre, so the letters of added plus are shifted around

explanation.surface: Readiness to ride is a bonus for a jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jockey' looks like a rider but is the verb to manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: Having fitted a saddle to the horse, one is prepared to mount and ride.

clue.text: Figure shut in dock suffering

parts.note: pent means penned or shut in

indicators.note: to dock is to cut off a tail, so the last letter of the suffering word goes

parts.note: agony is great suffering

explanation.surface: A shape is trapped in a harbour, in distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' looks like a harbour but means curtail.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-sided plane shape is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Puzzle about boat's return

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: the boat word comes back, read in the other direction

parts.note: a sub, short for submarine, is a boat

explanation.surface: A mystery concerning a vessel coming home.
explanation.definitionFit: A word puzzle shown in pictures or symbols, as in a picture riddle.

clue.text: One living alone before having child

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: Someone lived solitary until they had a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit, especially a religious recluse, lives apart from others.

clue.text: Troublemaker takes sword to tree with energy

parts.note: a fir is a conifer
E is the physics symbol for energy
brand is an old poetic word for sword

explanation.surface: A vandal energetically hacks at a tree with a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator who stirs up trouble, figuratively a burning torch.

clue.text: Water-bearing rock, one character voiced, is shaking

indicators.note: one letter is voiced: the unvoiced F becomes its voiced partner V

parts.note: an aquifer is rock holding groundwater

explanation.surface: Geology: a rock holding water, said aloud, trembles.
explanation.walkthrough: F and V are made the same way, but V uses the voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all of a quiver means trembling or shaking.

clue.text: Refrain from chapter on ancient deity

indicators.note: the deity comes on after the chapter letter

parts.note: Horus, the falcon-headed Egyptian god

explanation.surface: Avoid a book chapter about an old god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The repeated part of a song is its refrain.

clue.text: Undertake hazardous mission with ringing endorsement for success?

definitions.text: Undertake hazardous mission with ringing endorsement for success?

parts.words: Undertake hazardous mission with ringing endorsement for success?
parts.note: from the fable of the mice who wanted a bell hung on the cat; ringing hints at the bell

explanation.surface: Taking on a risky job with loud backing.
explanation.walkthrough: In the fable the mice agree to warn themselves by hanging a bell on the cat, but none dare do it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to take on a dangerous task for the common good.

clue.text: Do some knitting and babble

definitions.meaning: to flow with a murmur, as a brook does

explanation.surface: Knitting while chattering away.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a knitting stitch and the murmuring flow of a stream.

clue.text: Model one shouldn't miss

definitions.meaning: a person who poses for a portrait
an easy catch or shot, a sure thing

explanation.surface: A model you must not overlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a portrait painter's subject and an easy chance that ought to be taken.

clue.text: Deeply impressed, being serious in purpose

indicators.note: the serious word goes inside the purpose word

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose
grave means serious

explanation.surface: Someone was moved by an earnest sense of purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressed' is meant literally: cut into a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettering cut into a surface is literally deeply impressed.

clue.text: Last to look back

indicators.note: the look word is read back to front

parts.note: to peek is to look quickly

explanation.surface: The final one to glance behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to endure.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that will keep lasts without spoiling.

clue.text: Charge applied to contract with closely-arranged cover

indicators.note: the charge goes on after the other pieces

parts.note: to shrink is to contract
a rap is a criminal charge

explanation.surface: A fee is added to a contract for a tightly fitted covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic film shrunk tightly round goods is a close-fitting wrapping.
